title: Auto Loans: when a returned autopay debit is PCB's error because the paying account was closed
content:
# Auto Loans: when a returned autopay debit is PCB's error because the paying account was closed

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB decides whether a returned payment fee on an auto loan was assessed contrary to the Auto Loans charter because of how PCB presented an autopay debit.

## Clause

PCB keeps an autopay enrollment drawing only on a source account that is open on each debit date, extending to every debit the enrollment-time requirement that the autopay source be an active checking account of the borrower. Presenting a debit to an account that PCB's own records show already closed is therefore PCB's error, not the borrower's.

Accordingly, the returned payment fee is PCB's error when the returned payment was an autopay debit that PCB presented to a PCB checking account whose closing date on the borrower's checking records is **earlier than** the debit's posting date. It is not PCB's error when the returned payment was not an autopay debit, or when the paying account was still open on the debit's posting date or has no closing date.

## Truth table

| Returned payment was an autopay debit? | Paying account's closing date on the checking records | PCB's error? |
|---|---|---|
| yes | earlier than the debit's posting date | yes |
| yes | the same day as the posting date | no: still open on that date |
| yes | later than the posting date | no |
| yes | none | no |
| no | any | no |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical autopay debit posted 2026-06-05)

| Paying account closed on | PCB's error? |
|---|---|
| 2026-06-04 | yes: closed the day before the debit |
| 2026-06-05 | no: not earlier than the posting date |

## Points of judgement

**Does the borrower have to show that the account was closed?** No. The closing date is read from PCB's own checking records.
